headline: The S&P 500 is down about 3.7% into the close as the AI sell-off accelerates

findings.headline: S&P 500 down about 3.7% into the close, a 3.8-sigma day
findings.body: The S&P 500 was at 6,915 around 21:35 Zurich, down 3.7% on the day against a normal daily range of roughly 1%, with VIX at 35.5. Gold, copper, Brent and EUR/USD are barely moving, so this is an equity and AI-complex sell-off rather than a broad cross-asset scramble. The AI and chip unwind has now run for seven straight sessions, the longest losing streak since 2020.

sources.label: AP: S&P 500 drops as the AI sell-off accelerates

findings.headline: Wall Street picks up Europe's AI unwind, and Anthropic is now caught in it
findings.body: Anthropic fell about 9% in its first full session, back below its $97.17 debut close, as Nvidia and AMD extended their losses, so the record listing has not revived the AI trade. Leading and lagging on Wall Street is split the same way as in Europe: AI-heavy tech is lagging while old-economy Dow names hold up. MarketWatch notes the S&P 500 is heading for its longest losing streak since 2020.

MarketWatch: S&P 500 heads for longest losing streak since 2020

findings.headline: Norwegian gas supply tightens just as a cold snap arrives
findings.body: Equinor's Visund outage (13.2 mcm/day) has been extended to 1 January for fire repairs, and with cuts at Troll and Aasgard, Gassco data show Norwegian exports at 285.7 mcm/day against 335 mcm/day earlier this week. LSEG sees northwest European heating demand rising to 759 GWh/day next week from 528 GWh/day today, with storage at 69.8%, the lowest for the date since at least 2011. That combination means larger withdrawals from an already thin buffer heading into December.

sources.label: Reuters via Longbridge: Europe gas prices rise on tight supply, colder weather
ANSA: gas rises to 87 euro at the TTF

view: Our view: this is a stress day for equities alone, with metals, oil and the dollar calm, so it reads as AI-driven de-risking rather than a macro break. the US open confirmed the day's tone rather than resetting it. With a December hike fully priced, relief probably needs a soft PCE print next week; until then AI-heavy growth and precious metals stay the laggards, while Norway's supply cuts leave European gas as the one area where the risk is to the upside going into the cold snap.
